newsitem.title: CANADA: MacMillan says losses threaten B.C. industry.
newsitem.headline: MacMillan says losses threaten B.C. industry.

text.p: British Columbia's forest industry is in jeopardy unless it starts generating consistent earnings that equal its cost of capital, MacMillan Bloedel Ltd Chief Executive Robert Findlay said on Tuesday.

Speaking at an industry conference, Findlay said that in the current climate shareholders are reluctant to see any excess cash reinvested in the business. This, he said, "is a formula for disaster for the industry."

"I think that's the real threat to British Columbia and to those of us who work in the industry," he said. "If we don't earn the cost of capital, if we don't get a return for shareholders...slowly we'll die off."
MacMillan, Canada's biggest forest products company, has come under intense pressure from institutional shareholders who have been disappointed with its lagging performance.

Findlay said it was important for British Columbia companies to become low-cost producers. Many industry executives blame new regulations and government fees for increasing logging costs by about 70 percent since 1992.
Forest companies are in negotiations with the provincial government in hopes of winning some regulatory relief and to satisfy the government's calls for more forest-industry jobs.
Findlay, one of the company executives participating in the talks, said the process would likely conclude this month.
The outcome will be crucial in determining the outlook for the province's forest companies. "Then we will know whether we can go forward with optimism or not," he said.

Asked about a wave of consolidation among forest companies internationally, Findlay said he supported the trend. "I do think it's a good thing and, yes, I do think it's inevitable," he said. "I think it's the way of the future and I think we will see more of it."
